mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within the last month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to a decrease in S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are not significantly lower in periods following a >0.5% increase in FEDFUNDS (t-test p > 0.05), or if the Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate by more than 0.3 percentage points within the last month signals an improving labor market, which typically leads to an increase in S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are not significantly higher in periods following a >0.3pp decrease in UNRATE (t-test p > 0.05), or if the Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real estate sales (HOUST) over the last two months signals a strengthening demand in the housing market, which typically leads to an increase in S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are not significantly higher in periods following a sustained increase in HOUST (t-test p > 0.05), or if the Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% within the last two months signals an increase in economic activity, which typically leads to an increase in S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are not significantly higher in periods following a >1% increase in INDPRO (t-test p > 0.05), or if the Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in the last month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.2 percentage points, it signals a strong labor market, which typically leads to an increase in S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increase > 200k and UNRATE decrease > 0.2pp in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are not significantly higher in periods following the joint trigger conditions (t-test p > 0.05), or if the Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real GDP (GDPC1) over the last six months signals a strengthening economy, which typically leads to an increase in S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are not significantly higher in periods following a sustained increase in GDPC1 (t-test p > 0.05), or if the Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 5% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in the last month, it signals inflationary pressure, which typically leads to a decrease in S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 5% and CPIAUCSL increase > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are not significantly lower in periods following the joint trigger conditions (t-test p > 0.05), or if the Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in retail and food services sales (RSAFS) by more than 1% within the last month signals a weakening consumer demand, which typically leads to a decrease in S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are not significantly lower in periods following a >1% decrease in RSAFS (t-test p > 0.05), or if the Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.
